chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) awaiting renal transplantation with significant cardiovascular comorbidities and metabolic syndrome.
history_of_present_illness: 78‑year‑old woman with lifelong hypertension, obesity, and metabolic syndrome. CKD progressed from stage 2 to stage 4; listed for kidney transplant since 1994. Longstanding ischemic heart disease diagnosed in the 1970s, aortic valve replacement in 1984 with persistent aortic regurgitation. Chronic anemia, proteinuria secondary to type 2 diabetes, and prediabetes documented. Uses warfarin, hydrochlorothiazide, insulin, and nitroglycerin. Recent vital signs, renal labs, lipid panel, and glycemic trends are missing. Social factors include part‑time employment, intimate partner abuse history, criminal record, and poor dental health, potentially affecting adherence and transplant eligibility.

active_problems.name: Proteinuria due to type 2 diabetes mellitus

past_medical_history: Remote miscarriage (1949). Progressive CKD (stages 2‑4). Diabetes‑related kidney disorder with microalbuminuria. Chronic sinusitis, multiple dental extractions, prior acute bronchitis, and periods of full‑time employment. No documented resolution of hypertension or cardiovascular disease.

active_medications.name: Warfarin sodium 5 mg oral tablet
active_medications.purpose: Anticoagulation, likely for mechanical aortic valve prosthesis or prior thromboembolic event

active_medications.name: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg oral tablet
active_medications.purpose: Blood pressure control for essential hypertension

active_medications.name: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg/actuat mucosal spray
active_medications.purpose: Relief of angina related to ischemic heart disease

social_determinants: History of intimate partner abuse, part‑time employment, criminal record, higher education, poor dental health, and limited social support, all of which may impact medication adherence and transplant eligibility.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: high (ischemic heart disease, hypertension, valvular disease, obesity, metabolic syndrome, age >70). Renal risk: high (CKD stage 4, hypertension, proteinuria, diabetes, warfarin). Metabolic risk: elevated (obesity, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes). Hematologic risk: moderate (anemia of chronic disease/CKD). Neurologic risk: increased (advanced age plus vascular disease). Patient is at elevated risk for myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke, progression to end‑stage renal disease, and diabetes complications.

data_quality_flags.issue: Missing systolic blood pressure; cannot assess hypertension control.
BMI not recorded; obesity inferred from diagnosis only.
Recent estimated glomerular filtration rate not available; limits CKD staging precision.

clinical_impression: Elderly female with advanced CKD awaiting transplant, multiple high‑risk cardiovascular comorbidities, and metabolic syndrome; overall clinical picture dominated by renal and cardiovascular risk, with potential barriers to transplant related to social determinants and incomplete recent laboratory data.
